canonical.title: Which OpenAPI client generator for itenium-ui in 2026: Orval vs Hey API vs Kiota vs openapi-typescript

sources.title: ASP.NET Core OpenAPI support (learn.microsoft.com)
sources.claim: .NET 10 emits OpenAPI 3.1 by default (JSON Schema draft 2020-12); ProducesProblem/ProducesValidationProblem/TypedResults.Problem add the ProblemDetails response metadata.

sources.title: The .NET 10 OpenAPI number quirk (svrooij.io)
sources.claim: .NET 10 emits numeric properties as a string|integer union with a regex pattern, poisoning every generated TypeScript client; fix with JsonNumberHandling.Strict or a schema transformer.

sources.title: dotnet/aspnetcore#62099 — ProblemDetails extensions missing from schema
sources.claim: .NET 10's generated ProblemDetails schema declares only the five RFC 7807 fields and no additionalProperties; closed as answered rather than fixed.

sources.title: The Query Options API — TkDodo
sources.claim: TanStack Query's maintainer argues queryOptions is the abstraction to reach for first and that a wrapper hook per endpoint is no longer the default advice.

sources.title: queryOptions — TanStack Query v5 reference
sources.claim: queryOptions is TanStack Query v5's official type-safe helper for sharing a query definition between hooks and imperative QueryClient methods.

sources.title: Orval — React Query guide
sources.claim: Orval's react-query mode generates one custom hook per operation plus a getXQueryKey() function and the bare fetcher.

sources.title: orval-labs/orval#1788 — suspense query options don't typecheck
sources.claim: Orval hand-rolls its option objects instead of calling TanStack's queryOptions helper; generated suspense option functions are unusable in useSuspenseQuery. Still open.

sources.title: Orval — custom axios mutator guide
sources.claim: Orval types the TError channel of its generated hooks through an ErrorType alias exported from the custom mutator.

sources.title: Orval — output configuration reference
sources.claim: Orval's mock: true generates MSW handlers and Faker data alongside the client.

sources.title: CVE-2026-24132 — NVD
sources.claim: CVSS 7.7: a malicious OpenAPI document can inject arbitrary TypeScript into Orval's generated mock files; fixed in 7.20.0 and 8.0.3.

sources.title: orval-labs/orval#1817 — OpenAPI 3.1 type arrays
sources.claim: Orval reads OpenAPI 3.1 type arrays and emits the resulting | null unions, so .NET 10's 3.1 nullability lands correctly.

sources.title: Hey API — TanStack Query plugin
sources.claim: Hey API's TanStack Query plugin emits queryOptions, infiniteQueryOptions, mutationOptions and queryKey functions rather than hooks.

sources.title: hey-api — generated react-query.gen.ts example
sources.claim: Hey API's generated output imports TanStack's real queryOptions helper and calls the SDK with throwOnError: true.

sources.title: hey-api — query-core use-type.ts
sources.claim: Hey API resolves the TError generic to the operation's generated error type when the spec declares error responses, falling back to DefaultError only when it declares none.

sources.title: hey-api/openapi-ts#1029 — throwOnError stringified the error body
sources.claim: Hey API's throwOnError once stringified the error body into Error.message, discarding the typed ProblemDetails at runtime; closed by PR #1098.

sources.title: hey-api/hey-api on GitHub
sources.claim: Hey API (@hey-api/openapi-ts) is MIT-licensed, ships 20+ plugins, and is used by Vercel, PayPal and AWS.

sources.title: Hey API — get started
sources.claim: Hey API's hosted Platform is optional — input accepts a local file or URL just as well as a hey-api/* registry reference.

sources.title: openapi-typescript — introduction
sources.claim: openapi-typescript supports OpenAPI 3.0 and 3.1 and emits runtime-free types only.

sources.title: openapi-fetch — docs
sources.claim: openapi-fetch is a 6 kB fetch wrapper that returns a { data, error } discriminated union, both sides typed from the spec.

sources.title: openapi-react-query — docs
sources.claim: openapi-react-query is a ~1 kB runtime wrapper over TanStack Query exposing queryOptions, useQuery, useSuspenseQuery, useInfiniteQuery and useMutation.

sources.title: openapi-react-query — src/index.ts
sources.claim: openapi-react-query's queryFn throws the parsed error body, and its query keys are branded DataTag<key, data, error>.

sources.title: microsoft/kiota on GitHub
sources.claim: Kiota's own README marks TypeScript/JavaScript as in preview across generation, abstractions, serialization and HTTP.

sources.title: Kiota — language support & maturity ladder
sources.claim: Preview means Kiota is near stable but isn't being used to generate production API clients.

sources.title: Kiota — TypeScript quickstart
sources.claim: Kiota generates a fluent request-builder client whose models are all-optional, and requires a Kiota-specific request adapter and auth provider.

sources.title: Kiota — install
sources.claim: Kiota ships as a binary download, a Docker image or a .NET global tool — there is no npm distribution.

sources.title: microsoft/kiota-typescript on GitHub
sources.claim: The TypeScript runtime libraries Kiota's generated clients depend on sit in a repo with 61 stars.

sources.title: Nx — commands reference (sync:check)
sources.claim: Nx's sync generators plus nx sync:check give a first-class way to fail CI when a generated artifact has drifted from its source.

sources.title: npm downloads — openapi-fetch
sources.claim: openapi-fetch drew 5.97M npm downloads in the week of 5-11 Jul 2026.

sources.title: npm downloads — @hey-api/openapi-ts
sources.claim: @hey-api/openapi-ts drew 2.88M npm downloads in the week of 5-11 Jul 2026; orval drew 1.29M and @microsoft/kiota-bundle 47.9k.

sources.title: openapi-ts/openapi-typescript on GitHub
sources.claim: openapi-typescript, openapi-fetch and openapi-react-query live in one monorepo under the openapi-ts org.
